Input selects the previous acknowledged actuator sample, applies copied controls and latches command arrays before physics. The feedback channel is delayed sample-and-hold, not a cyclic graph edge.

Physics dispatches nested bounded CPU tasks or the CUDA owner. Integer velocity then position update matches the independent full-state oracle. CUDA changes this phase only; publication waits for terminal completion.
Stage serializes complete position/velocity into fixed host-visible channel frames. The combined pipeline uses explicit host staging; device-local timelines do not establish peer DMA.
Sensor copies and validates the selected sample and applies the latched calibration. The XDMA variant consumes native backend sampled input with exact sequence, age and completion identity.

Controller computes bounded integer gain times velocity error, clamps acceleration to four and publishes a fixed command. An external controller runs in a separate process and supplies a copied snapshot; callbacks do no transport I/O.
Actuator encodes the command, with explicit zero effort on absent input. XDMA sampled output is safe only after an actual terminal acknowledgement; acceptance of submission alone is insufficient.
Aggregate sums each position/velocity axis from its selected channel snapshot into six int64 values. It does not read another active rate domain's live arrays.
Telemetry records bounded phase observations. Host code drains trace, rate and control streams after settled steps and writes evidence off lane. Exact loss invalidates the sample replay gate.

entries.explanation: The explicit acyclic dependency input to physics orders conflicting accesses within one rate domain. Cross-rate feedback uses copied channels and deterministic prior-record selection, not an added graph cycle.

contract.auxiliary_layout: Separate fixed SoA command[3][256] int32 and sensor[position,velocity][3][256] int32; each 64-byte aligned. Aggregate position/velocity axis sums use six int64 slots. Instance-local uint64 logical_tick, successful_steps, control_generation, sample_sequence[5], command_generation; checked increment with no wrap. Snapshot encodes fields individually, never native padding/pointers.
contract.controller: For each axis: clamp(gain*(target_velocity-sampled_velocity), -4, 4), int64 intermediate; gain default1 range0..4, target default8 range-64..64; calibrated sensor = raw+offset, offset default0 range-16..16
contract.initialization: M24 LCG uint32 wrap: state=1664525*state+1013904223; entity then axis, x=next%2049-1024, v=next%129-64, a=next%9-4; seed=1
contract.layout: SoA: field, axis, entity; unused entities zero
contract.oracle: M24 piecewise constant acceleration: v(n)=v0+n*a, x(n)=x0+n*v0+a*n*(n+1)/2; split at each acknowledged command change; compare every field of every entity, tolerance zero
contract.owner: one scenario instance; heap storage allocated before finalize
contract.rollback: Runtime generation rollback does not restore sample/backend state. A failed frame is terminal for this owner; checked settle/stop, then restore a paired successful checkpoint in a fresh owner.
contract.update: v_next=v+a; x_next=x+v_next; widen intermediates to int64, checked narrow to int32; no float or saturation in plant

entries.explanation: Each owner reserves fixed aligned SoA, command, sensor, frame, aggregate and canonical state storage before execution. Every field and auxiliary buffer layout is retained below. Application/Runtime checkpoints are paired only after a successful quiescent step; failed side effects require checked stop and fresh-owner recovery.

contract.epoch: logical zero; half-open [0,ticks*base_tick_ns); no wall-clock correctness oracle

entries.explanation: The 10 ms base tick is logical simulation time. The host Runtime clock, backend-local timeline and host benchmark steady clock are separate domains; compare timestamps only through explicit correlation. The owned simulator selects a finite 5 s scheduling watchdog while preserving 1 ms CUDA and 8 ms sampled logical/backend budgets. None is RT qualification.

contract.ordering: Rates in listed registration order, then compiled phase order, substep0; ordinary edges within a domain only; channels select latest preceding producer reference, including earlier same-time domains; first missing predecessor selects explicit initial, repeating horizon wraps to previous cycle.
contract.policy: Configure/finalize allocate; callbacks use fixed storage and bounded integer work only. Host control owns threads, clocks, files and drains. Keep borrowed memory/driver/host alive through acknowledged checked stop; failed cleanup retains ownership and invocation failure; no restart after stopped.
contract.staging: physics completion -> CPU stage copy -> sensor channel; no device/device channel or peer DMA; CUDA and XDMA timelines are backend-local; same scenario identities in all variants.

entries.explanation: Session borrows caller-owned jobs, arenas, clock and drivers; accepted work and failed checked stop extend those lifetimes. Prepare allocates/finalizes off lane. The bounded worker/task/queue/scratch/retention values below are frozen. Serialized host control drains telemetry and performs process/file I/O; callbacks do not.

contract.application_latch: Decode copied generation once per identity into sample-owned per-kind config; untouched kinds persist. Calibration offset changes application values only; fixed HAL calibration identity and descriptor never mutate. No Runtime payload parser or arbitrary application rollback.
contract.envelope: M22 RTLC v1, 32-byte canonical envelope plus 16-byte body; explicit little-endian fields, unused words zero
contract.ordering: Stage on non-RT host before exact target closes; resolve tick to compiled reference index/domain/phase/release/substep in first supercycle only. Use host-frame target for later-cycle controls, latched by host before its next step; never retarget a closed rate record. Sort mailbox then sequence; later same-kind replaces earlier; copy callback-local payload before return; never retain view.
contract.replay: Opt-in trusted M22 v2 admission/generation payload artifact plus M21 mixed-rate actions and sample-owned checkpoint. Reject gaps, changed contract/config/source, generation mismatch, malformed bytes or untrusted payload. Pair Runtime and application snapshots only at successful quiescent step boundary; replay mock/loopback only; never real-device side effects.

entries.explanation: Five fixed payload types use copied immutable generations and exact host/rate boundaries. The 16-slot mailbox rejects excess; same-kind replacement commits the last accepted record. Typed malformed controls are rejected off lane. Trusted replay stays on the originating simulated owner; source/configuration, generation and gap guards precede effects.

contract.drain: outside callbacks after each settled host step; snapshot before checked stop releases backing; no RT file I/O
contract.identity: scenario_id + canonical contract SHA256 + source commit/tree + configuration digest + variant + host + fresh session generation
contract.loss: report sequence gaps/dropped/overwritten separately; any loss invalidates deterministic replay, never silently fabricate payloads

entries.explanation: Trace, rate, mixed-rate and live-control records retain distinct schemas and cursor identities. Drain after settled steps, before backing storage release, on host control. Report dropped/overwritten/gap counts separately. Disabled capture is unavailable history, not a measured gap; any measured gap invalidates sample replay.

contract.protocol: Sample-owned M26 vector protocol v1; reuse M25 platform publication/ownership principles, never relabel the scalar M25 wire schema. Fixed 256x3 int32 velocity/command arrays, canonical LE, count and generation, sequence, issue/expiry tick, payload digest and zero unused entries. Encode off lane into fixed SPSC slots; CPU controller phase consumes copied snapshot only. Fresh mapping/name/generation on reconnect; one writer, no overwrite; stale/missing peer gives zero effort then fresh-owner recovery. Exact byte-offset codec is M26-02 implementation acceptance, not an extension of any SDK ABI.

entries.explanation: The M26 vector transport owns a fresh mapping and generation per session, fixed 256 by 3 int32 arrays and one writer per channel. The actual external process supplies bounded snapshots. A missing or expired peer produces zero effort, then fresh-mapping/fresh-owner recovery; no callback spins on IPC or filesystem work.
